cards.heading: Definition
cards.question: What does the MCP feature lifecycle policy (SEP-2577/2596) guarantee?
cards.answer: Every protocol feature follows Active → Deprecated → Removed, with at least twelve months between deprecation and earliest removal, and removal itself requires a separate SEP — so implementers can build on a version knowing what they ship keeps working.

cards.heading: The conformance-suite gate
cards.question: What conformance-suite gate keeps a Standards-Track SEP from silently becoming a breaking change?
cards.answer: A Standards-Track SEP can no longer reach Final status until a matching scenario lands in the conformance suite — the same suite the SDK tier system scores official SDKs against, turning 'the spec says' into 'the suite checks'.

cards.heading: Three governance mechanisms together
cards.question: Besides the lifecycle policy itself, what other two governance mechanisms does the same MCP release install so breaking changes stay exceptional?
cards.answer: The extensions framework, which lets new capabilities stabilise outside core; and the conformance-suite gate that blocks Standards-Track SEPs from reaching Final without a matching test scenario.

cards.heading: Worked example: the three deprecated features
cards.question: Which three core MCP features did the release immediately deprecate, and what happens to them in the meantime?
cards.answer: Roots (replaced by tool parameters, resource URIs, or configuration), Sampling (direct LLM-provider integration), and Logging (stderr for stdio, OpenTelemetry for structured). All three are annotation-only deprecations — methods and capability flags keep working in this release and every version published within a year.

cards.heading: The transferable pattern
cards.question: What is the transferable pattern behind this policy, applicable to any protocol?
cards.answer: Pair a dated deprecation window with named replacements and a conformance gate — that lets a protocol evolve aggressively at the edges while staying safe to build on at the core.
